shower.thought: We spend our whole lives learning how to be ourselves, and by the time we figure it out, we're supposed to stop.
The people who need apologies the most are usually the least likely to accept them.
You can tell how insecure someone is by how much they talk about their accomplishments.
Nostalgia is just your brain editing out all the parts that sucked.
We call it "falling in love" but we're really just choosing our favorite obsession.
The more you know about something, the less impressive it becomes—except for things worth knowing about.
You're probably not as unique as you think, but you're definitely not as ordinary as you worry you are.
Patience isn't about waiting longer—it's about deciding the wait is worth it.
We fear rejection more than we actually value acceptance.
The people you envy are envying someone too.
You can't authentically connect with someone while you're performing for them.
Most arguments aren't about who's right—they're about who gets to feel right.
Your body keeps score of things your mind forgot to process.
We inherit our parents' fear more than we inherit their dreams.
The saddest part about toxic people is that they're usually just broken people nobody fixed in time.
You don't need closure—you just need permission to leave.
The things that make you cringe about yourself are often the things nobody else remembers.
We confuse being busy with being productive, and busy with being important.
Your standards for others reveal your standards for yourself.
Silence between two people says more than words ever could.

Discipline is just choosing between what you want now and what you want most. — Unknown
Your life doesn't improve by chance; it improves by change. — Ralph Marston
The person you're becoming is worth every uncomfortable moment. — Unknown
Regret weighs more than effort ever will. — Unknown
You're not behind. You're exactly where you need to be to become who you're meant to be. — Unknown
Small steps taken consistently will always outrun giant leaps taken sporadically. — Unknown
The only approval that matters is the one you give yourself. — Unknown
Comfort is a beautiful prison. — Unknown
You don't rise to the level of your goals; you fall to the level of your systems. — James Clear
The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago. The second best time is now. — Chinese Proverb
What you resist persists. What you accept begins to transform. — Unknown
Most people fail not because they can't, but because they stop before they see proof that they can. — Unknown
Your scars are proof that you've survived everything up to this point. — Unknown
The life you're waiting for requires the version of you that you haven't built yet. — Unknown
Fear and excitement are the same chemical reaction. One just has a different story attached. — Unknown
You're not looking for motivation. You're looking for permission. Here it is. — Unknown
The cost of discipline is always less than the cost of regret. — Unknown
What would you attempt if you knew you absolutely could not fail? Start there. — Unknown
The best investment you can make is in yourself. Interest compounds. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
My girlfriend asked why I never want to meet her parents.
I said, "I like to keep some mystery alive in our relationship."
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

The doctor told me I had six months to live.
I couldn't pay the bill, so he gave me another six months.

My therapist asked if I had any skeletons in my closet.
I said, "Not anymore—I finally organized them by height."

I told my boss I was going through a rough patch.
He said, "At least you're going through something."

My wife's leaving me because I'm "obsessed with the future."
Wait till she sees what I've got planned.
I'm not saying my childhood was bad, but my imaginary friend left me.

People say I have a dark sense of humor.
I say they just can't appreciate the finer things in life, like a well-timed funeral joke.

My son asked me why I cried at his school play.
I said, "Because you're going to remember this confidence forever, and it's going to hurt so much."

I told my dentist my teeth were killing me.
He said, "Not yet, but I'm working on it."

My friend said depression runs in his family.
I said, "So does everything else when you stop paying the mortgage."

I asked my dad how he stayed so thin his whole life.
He said, "Cigarettes and broken promises."
Turns out it was mostly just the first one.

My therapist says I'm avoiding my problems.
I said, "That's ridiculous," and changed the subject to something cheerful, like mortality.

I told my mom I was having an existential crisis.
She said, "That's nice, honey. When you're done, there's laundry in the basement."

My coworker asked if I believed in life after death.
I said, "I don't even believe in life after Monday."

I gave up on my New Year's resolution to lose weight.
Turns out my real resolution was just to accept myself. That lasted about three days.

My priest said I was going to Hell.
I said, "At least it's somewhere warm. Have you seen my heating bill?"

I told my kid that Santa isn't real.
He cried for an hour. Then I told him about taxes and he understood.

My therapist asked what my biggest fear was.
I said, "That one day I'll finally get my life together and realize it was never worth the effort."

I told my date I was really into deep conversations.
Turns out she meant emotionally, not literally.
